title: The Abbott and Costello Show
paragraphs: Comedy-variety archive centered on Bud Abbott and Lou Costello. Descriptive file titles are archive labels, not official historical episode titles.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Kate Smith appearances (February 3, 1938 to June 28, 1940) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Time to Smile (July 3, 1940 to September 25, 1940) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Chase and Sanborn appearances (April 6, 1941 to June 28, 1942) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and NBC Camel years (October 8, 1942 to June 26, 1947) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Bud Abbott (performer), Lou Costello (performer), Ken Niles (announcer and performer), Connie Haines (performer and vocalist), Freddie Rich and His Orchestra (performer), Elvia Allman (performer), and Mel Blanc (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.66865a83f6609315|KFI]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], and [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

The stories often return to Hollywood, movies and celebrity guests, everyday jobs, money and domestic mishaps, music and variety performance, detective and crime parody, western parody and frontier comedy, and wartime service, military and home-front comedy.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Sponsor-driven network comedy, Wartime popular comedy and service culture, Hollywood guest-star variety culture, and Postwar shift to transcribed/cooperative network radio.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|sealtest-variety-theater|Sealtest Variety Theater]], and [[show|the-phil-harris-alice-faye-show|The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show]].
